questions.prompt: The Suspensory Act 1914 was a UK law whose sole purpose was to postpone the coming into force of two other acts due to the outbreak of World War I. Which two acts did it suspend?
choices: The Government of Ireland Act 1914 and the Welsh Church Act 1914
The Parliament Act 1911 and the Official Secrets Act 1911
The Defence of the Realm Act 1914 and the Aliens Restriction Act 1914
The Representation of the People Act 1918 and the Sex Disqualification Act 1919
questions.hint: The correct answer involves two acts passed in the same year as the Suspensory Act itself, one concerning Irish self-governance and the other concerning religious disestablishment in Wales.
questions.explanation: The Suspensory Act 1914 was enacted to delay the implementation of the Government of Ireland Act 1914 (Irish Home Rule) and the Welsh Church Act 1914 (disestablishment of the Church in Wales) because of the outbreak of World War I.

questions.prompt: The Wikipedia article on 'Ley de fugas' describes a practice where prisoners were allowed to run as if escaping, giving authorities an excuse to shoot them for trying to flee. Under Spanish colonial rule in the Philippines, this method was used to execute a group of Katipunan-linked patriots known as the Martyrs of Bicol in 1897. How many martyrs made up this group?
questions.hint: The number is fewer than 10... actually, think a bit higher, somewhere close to 10-15.
questions.explanation: The article notes that the ley de fugas was employed by Spanish colonial authorities in the Philippines, including in the execution of the Thirteen Martyrs of Bicol in 1897, a group of 13 people accused of supporting the Katipunan revolt.

questions.prompt: A certain Cyrillic letter looks exactly the same as the Latin letter S, making it the ultimate weapon in IDN homograph attacks. Which of the following is that real unusual article about a letter?
questions.hint: It's not 'Dzo' or 'Zhwe', those aren't real Cyrillic letters at all.
questions.explanation: Dze is a letter of the Cyrillic alphabet that visually resembles the Latin letter S, which can be exploited in phishing attacks using deceptive domain names.

questions.prompt: George P. Burdell is a fictitious student who has been continuously enrolled at Georgia Tech since a certain year, aside from his 'service' in World War II. In what year was he officially enrolled?
questions.hint: It's not 1930, when he supposedly graduated, nor 1945, around the end of World War II.
questions.explanation: George P. Burdell was fictitiously enrolled at Georgia Tech in 1927 as a prank by student Ed Smith, and has remained continuously enrolled ever since, except for his 'service' during World War II.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is a real unusual legal case, sometimes nicknamed the 'Ghostbusters case,' in which a court ruled that a house in Nyack, New York was legally haunted by ghosts?
questions.hint: The correct case does not involve the surnames Whitfield, Marlowe, Pemberton, Halloway, Caldwell, or Renshaw.
questions.explanation: In this real court case, a New York judge ruled that a house was legally considered haunted because the seller had publicly claimed it was, allowing the buyer to rescind the purchase contract.

questions.prompt: The Wikipedia article 'Phantom ballplayer' describes players who appear on MLB rosters or records without ever actually playing, or who never existed at all. Which name was fraudulently inserted into a 1912 St. Louis Browns box score as a joke, giving him two plate appearances in official records for decades before he was removed?
questions.hint: It's not the man famous for a single real at-bat as a publicity stunt, nor the player immortalized in 'Field of Dreams,' nor the legendary manager.
questions.explanation: Lou Proctor was fraudulently credited with two plate appearances in a 1912 box score, likely as a prank by a Western Union operator, and remained in official records for decades until MLB removed him in the 1980s.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is a real unusual article about an international contest between pigs?
questions.hint: The real event does not involve yoga or beauty judging, so you can rule out the goat and cow competitions.
questions.explanation: The Pig Olympics was an international competition in which pigs from different countries competed in events like racing and swimming.

questions.prompt: Before becoming synonymous with video games, Nintendo dabbled in unusual side projects, including an educational software title called 'I Am a Teacher: Super Mario Sweater.' What activity did this Nintendo product actually teach players?
questions.hint: It's not a culinary or paper craft skill, it's a domestic skill often associated with making clothing items like sweaters.
questions.explanation: 'I Am a Teacher: Super Mario Sweater' was an unusual Nintendo educational title that taught players how to knit, using Mario-themed patterns as part of the lesson.

questions.prompt: According to Balkan legend, fruits left outside on a night of the full moon could be turned by vampires, leaving behind blood-red streaks. Which of the following is a real unusual Wikipedia article about this folklore?
questions.hint: The correct article is not about cabbages or wheat; it involves fruits commonly found on a fall harvest table.
questions.explanation: In Balkan folklore, pumpkins and watermelons left outside for too long, especially during a full moon, were believed to become vampires, with their reddish streaks seen as a telltale sign of demonic possession.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is a real piece of legislation that, despite seeming like an innocuous piece of congressional business, became the subject of outrageous but widely believed conspiracy theories in 1956?
questions.hint: The real act is not the 'Federal Mental Institution Relocation Act' or the 'Alaska Public Health Reform Act', those are fabricated titles.
questions.explanation: The Alaska Mental Health Enabling Act of 1956 was a routine bill meant to improve mental health services in the Alaska Territory, but it sparked widespread conspiracy theories claiming it would be used to imprison political dissidents in secret asylums.
